summary: The app adapter must return one result for each of q moves, while the protected deque and occupancy-set design performs expected constant work per move.

optimality.argument: Reading q directions and returning q results requires linear work, and the protected implementation matches that lower bound with expected constant work for each move.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any correct app-local solution must read all q requested directions and emit q score or game-over results, establishing an Omega(q) time lower bound.

Each protected move performs a fixed number of coordinate, food, deque, and expected constant-time hash-set operations. Across q calls this proves expected O(q) time and O(f) state, where the snake can grow at most once for each food item.

Independent direct checks verify the complete source example, repeated length-one tail movement, growth through all food, collision with a non-tail body cell, legal entry into a departing tail cell, and persistent -1 results after game over.
